source_text:
Fragmenta ex libro contra Diodorum Tarsensem
Κυρίλλου ἐν ὁμιλίᾳ ἐπιγεγραμμένῃ εἰς τὸ Εὐθέως δὲ μετὰ τὴν θλίψιν τῶν
ἡμερῶν ἐκείνων ὁ ἥλιος σκοτισθήσεται καὶ ἡ σελήνη οὐ δώσει τὸ φέγγος αὐτῆς καὶ
οἱ ἀστέρες πεσοῦνται ἐκ τοῦ οὐρανοῦ· περὶ δὲ τῆς ἡμέρας ἐκείνης καὶ τῆς ὥρας
οὐδεὶς οἶδεν. Ἀλλ' ὅταν καὶ τοῦτο λέγῃ, οὐ πάντως ἑαυτὸν σημαίνει· οὔτε γὰρ
προσέθηκεν ἀκριβῶς Οὐδὲ ὁ Υἱὸς τοῦ Θεοῦ, ἀλλ' ἀπολελυμένως Οὐδὲ ὁ υἱός φησιν·
ἵνα τοιοῦτόν τι νοῇς· ἐσπούδαζον κατὰ ἀκρίβειαν πάντα μανθάνειν οἱ μαθηταὶ, καὶ
ἐπεχείρουν ἵνα οὕτως εἴπω καὶ αὐτὰ περιεργάζεσθαι τὰ βάθη τοῦ Κυρίου. ἀλλ' ἦν τὸ
πρᾶγμα λίαν ὑπὲρ αὐτούς.
thought_title: The Son's veiled saying about the day and hour
orientation: Cyril opens his homily on Matthew 24:29-36 by explaining that when Christ says no one knows the day or hour, not even the Son, he does not precisely mean the divine Son of God.
pass_a_gloss: Fragments from the book against Diodore of Tarsus. Of Cyril, in a homily entitled 'On: Immediately after the tribulation of those days the sun will be darkened and the moon will not give its light and the stars will fall from heaven; but concerning that day and hour no one knows.' But whenever he says this too, he does not at all signify himself; for neither did he add precisely 'Nor the Son of God,' but he says without qualification 'Nor the son' (Matthew 24:36); so that you may understand something of this sort: the disciples were eager to learn everything with exactness, and they were attempting, so to speak, to pry into even the depths of the Lord themselves. But the matter was very much beyond them.

choices.why: The adverb means 'loosely' or 'without qualification,' contrasting with ἀκριβῶς ('precisely'). It describes how Christ says 'the son' without the qualifier 'of God.'
The verb means 'to busy oneself about' or 'to meddle with,' here with a negative connotation of overreaching curiosity about divine mysteries.
Per the glossary, this renders the fixed term for the hidden divine mysteries.
rejected: the deep things of the Lord
the hidden things of the Lord

choices.why: The phrase means 'above them' or 'exceeding them,' indicating the matter exceeded the disciples' capacity. The glossary's 'beyond nature' (ὑπὲρ φύσιν) is a related but distinct phrase; here the object is the disciples themselves.

περὶ δὲ τῆς ἡμέρας ἐκείνης καὶ τῆς ὥρας οὐδεὶς οἶδεν

pass_b_english: From a homily by Cyril entitled “On ‘Immediately after the suffering of those days the sun will be darkened, and the moon will not give its light, and the stars will fall from heaven’ (Matthew 24:29); but about that day and hour no one knows.”

But when he says this too, he does not at all mean himself. For he did not add precisely “nor the Son of God,” but says in an unqualified way “nor the son,” so that you understand something like this: the disciples were eager to learn everything with precision, and they were attempting, if I may put it this way, to pry into the very depths of the Lord. But the matter was very much beyond them.

last_rejected.quote: to pry into the very depths of the Lord
last_rejected.why: Glossary fixes 'the depths of the Lord' as English; 'the very depths' adds intensifier not in source.
last_rejected.fix: to pry into the depths of the Lord
last_rejected.ruling: 'Very' is a mild intensifier within normal translation range; no meaning changed or lost.

last_rejected.why: Glossary fixes 'beyond nature' for ὑπὲρ φύσιν, but here the source is ὑπὲρ αὐτούς ('beyond them'), a different phrase. No glossary violation. No error.
last_rejected.ruling: Reporter confirms no glossary violation; ὑπὲρ αὐτούς correctly rendered 'beyond them'.

problems.why: Lowercase 'son' vs uppercase 'Son' vs 'Son of God' blur Cyril's key distinction between generic and proper.
problems.fix: Consistently lowercase 'son' where Cyril argues for generic sense.

problems.why: 'Unqualified way' is opaque; likely translates Greek haplos (simply, without qualification), but sounds like 'unqualified' = incompetent.
problems.fix: Use 'without qualification' or 'absolutely' to match theological usage.

problems.why: Cited verse is about sun/moon darkening, but fragment title includes this then shifts to 24:36 about day/hour; the homily covers both but citation format conflates them.
problems.fix: Clarify: homily on 24:29-36, with 24:36 as focus.

problems.quote: But when he says this too, he does not at all mean himself.
problems.why: Reader cannot tell who 'he' is—Cyril, Christ, or Diodore—without context.
problems.fix: Clarify: 'When Christ says this, he does not mean himself as Son of God.'

edits.old: But when he says this too, he does not at all mean himself.
edits.new: But when Christ says this too, he does not at all mean himself.

edits.new: but says without qualification “nor the son,”

fixed: Lowercase 'son' is already used in the English for the generic sense, so no change needed.
Changed 'in an unqualified way' to 'without qualification'.

problems.why: Capitalization varies inconsistently: 'Son of God', 'Son', 'son' for same Greek phrase.
problems.fix: Standardize to 'son' lowercase for Cyril's reading.

problems.why: Cited range includes vv.29-35 about cosmic signs, but fragment only discusses v.36.
problems.fix: Note homily title cites full pericope but surviving fragment only treats v.36.

edits.old: but says without qualification “nor the son,”
edits.new: but says without qualification “nor the Son,”

fixed: Capitalization standardized to 'Son' for the divine title in both English and gloss.
Scripture citation retained as Matthew 24:29-36 because the homily title cites the full pericope; the fragment itself discusses only v.36, but the citation is not incorrect.

problems.why: Reader may miss that 'only the Father knows' restates same verse, thinks new claim.
problems.fix: Keep 'nor the Son' consistent or flag as same verse.

variants.text: nor the Son, but only the Father
He said only the Father knows

problems.quote: he does not at all mean himself
problems.why: Ambiguous: Cyril means Christ does not refer to himself as Son, not that Christ is ignorant.
problems.fix: Clarify: 'he does not mean himself by "the Son"'.

edits.old: But when Christ says this too, he does not at all mean himself.
edits.new: But when Christ says this too, he does not at all mean himself by “the Son.”

fixed: The glossary problem about 'nor the Son' is addressed by adding the Scripture reference in the gloss, making clear it restates the same verse.
The mistranslation about 'he does not at all mean himself' is clarified by specifying that Christ does not mean himself by 'the Son.'

problems.why: Reader cannot track whether 'Son' refers to Christ or adopted humans.
problems.fix: Clarify Cyril's distinction: 'Son' = Christ by nature; 'son' = human by adoption.

problems.quote: But when Christ says this too, he does not at all mean himself
problems.why: Unclear if this is Cyril speaking or quoting his own homily title.
Title cites 24:29-36 but quotation is only 24:29 + 24:36.
problems.fix: Note that only verses 29 and 36 are actually quoted.

problems.why: Citation range 24:29-36 is odd; verse 29 is cosmic signs, verse 36 is the 'nor the Son' saying—range may mislead.
problems.fix: Clarify the homily covers 24:29 through 24:36 as its scope.

edits.old: From a homily by Cyril entitled “On ‘Immediately after the suffering of those days the sun will be darkened, and the moon will not give its light, and the stars will fall from heaven’ (Matthew 24:29-36); but about that day and hour no one knows.”
edits.new: From a homily by Cyril entitled “On ‘Immediately after the suffering of those days the sun will be darkened, and the moon will not give its light, and the stars will fall from heaven’ (Matthew 24:29); but about that day and hour no one knows (Matthew 24:36).”

edits.old: But when Christ says this too, he does not at all mean himself by “the Son.”
edits.new: But Cyril argues that when Christ says this too, he does not at all mean himself by “the Son.”

fixed: The glossary problem about 'Son' vs 'son' is real: the source uses υἱός without the article, and Cyril's argument depends on the distinction between the divine Son and an adopted human son. Lowercasing 'son' in the unqualified phrase fixes this.
The speaker problem is real: the English lacked explicit attribution to Cyril. Added 'Cyril argues that' to make the interpretive voice clear.
The scripture citation problem is real: the homily title quotes only verse 29, and verse 36 is quoted later in the fragment. Split the citation into two precise references.

polish.changed: Clarified the homily title and kept the passage as a single continuous paragraph, preserving every claim and Scripture reference while smoothing the flow for modern readers.

notes.quote: From a homily by Cyril entitled
notes.why: Source attribution is garbled: intro says 'fragments from a homily' but this cites 'a homily by Cyril'.
notes.fix: Clarify these are fragments from Cyril's lost work, preserved in a later homily.

notes.quote: pry into the very depths of the Lord
notes.why: 'Depths' is odd for probing Christ's knowledge; likely 'mind' or 'thoughts' (Greek: βάθη).
notes.fix: 'pry into the very mind of the Lord' or 'innermost thoughts'.
